subject: Starnet dedicated pool — graceful degradation, mitigation, and next steps

Subject: Starnet dedicated pool — graceful degradation, mitigation, and next steps

Laura / Starnet ops team,

Quick incident summary in plain terms and immediate actions we took — I wanted to make sure you had a single-threaded view while we investigate the root cause: 

What happened (impact):
- Between 06:45–07:00 PT the dedicated GPU pool serving Starnet spiked to 3x baseline concurrency. A provisioning controller job used for the autoscaler stalled while reconciling instance templates, which prevented new reserved nodes from attaching.
- Result: sustained queueing for long-running generation requests for ~18 minutes, and elevated token latency for a subset (~12%) of requests. No customer data was exposed.

Immediate mitigation we ran:
- Activated graceful-degradation profile for Starnet: reduced max_concurrency per-tenant by 40% and automatically routed low-priority work to the cold-fallback model (routed users to m-small variant) to preserve 95th percentile latency for interactive flows.
- Manually cleared the stuck provisioning job and restarted the autoscaler; new nodes began attaching at 07:10 PT.
- Applied temporary per-tenant request shaping to prevent retries from overloading the queue.

What we're doing next (short term):
- Full post-incident runbook and a timeline doc attached. We're preparing a short RCA and a set of configuration changes to make the autoscaler reconciler more robust.
- We'll share the postmortem and a suggested credit calculation for the affected window by EOD PT.

Attachments: starnet_incident_timeline.pdf (timeline + metrics), mitigation-runbook.md (temporary ops steps used).

Apologies for the disruption — keeping this thread as the canonical source. If you need an immediate bridge, I can stand up a 30-min call now.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Starnet dedicated pool — graceful degradation, mitigation, and next steps

Evelyn — thanks for the heads up and for the quick mitigation. Short internal note / next actions from ops: 

- Autoscaler reconciler root cause: our preliminary trace shows a race in the instance template update path when two simultaneous scaling signals occur for the same allocation group. The second reconcile occasionally times out and leaves an orphaned state.
- Temporary config we applied: increased reconcile timeout to 90s and moved the reconcile backoff to 2s -> 5s to reduce thrash.
- Action items (owners):
  - Karthik: A/B test the new reconcile backoff on a canary pool and add an abort-and-recreate path for stuck updates (ETA: 48 hours).
  - Ben: Validate tenant request shaping doesn't impact billing tokens; ensure metrics still count correctly and add an alert for shaping-triggered events (ETA: 24 hours).
  - Marissa: Prepare canary runbook and coordinate a one-hour maintenance window with Starnet if the fix requires a rolling restart of the reconciler (ETA: propose window today).

I'll also collect the raw reconciler logs and put them in the shared drive link Evelyn included.

—Marissa
Director, Dedicated Capacity Ops
Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident summary: Starnet dedicated pool — RCA, mitigation, and credit proposal

Laura / Starnet team,

Short post-incident summary and next steps (single doc attached): postmortem-dedicated-pool-20270426.pdf

Root cause (brief):
- A race in our autoscaler reconciler caused a subset of instance-template updates to enter an orphaned state when two concurrent scale signals targeted the same allocation group. The reconciler's abort path did not trigger due to a timeout condition in the controller (we have since increased the timeout and added an explicit abort-and-recreate step).

Work completed so far: 
- Restarted the reconciler and removed the stuck job (07:10 PT).
- Increased reconcile timeout and adjusted backoff parameters to reduce thrash (Marissa validated canary behavioral changes).
- Implemented a short-term shaping policy to protect the control plane and prevent cascading retries.

Planned follow-ups (owners & ETA):
- Karthik: Deploy abort-and-recreate reconciler patch to canary pool (ETA: 48 hours), followed by staged rollout to production.
- Marissa: Add an alert that triggers when reconcile durations exceed 60s and track failed-update counts per allocation group (ETA: 24 hours).
- Ben: Validate billing reconciliation for shaped requests and prepare a token-level reconciliation report for Starnet (ETA: 72 hours).

Credit proposal: 
- We propose a one-time goodwill credit equivalent to 10% of the billed token consumption for the affected hour (06:45–07:45 PT). If you prefer a usage-based reconciliation, Ben will run a token-by-token diff and share a reconciled figure.

Attachments included: postmortem-dedicated-pool-20270426.pdf, starnet_incident_timeline.pdf, mitigation-runbook.md

Links: https://redwood-drive.internal/shared/starnet-incident-20270426
HubSpot record: HUBSPOT-123456

If this looks good, Evelyn and I can schedule a 30-min walkthrough for your reviewers this afternoon at 1:30pm PT.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
